sentiment: Old locks give way to patient minds, and the smallest threads hold the heaviest days together.

stories.title: Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
stories.summary: A 370-year-old cipher sat unread because no one was left who cared enough to keep turning it over — and then a patient reader did, and three centuries of silence became a sentence. Some locks are not broken, only outlasted.

stories.title: Rope, twine and thread: Invisible technologies of the Stone Age
stories.summary: The technologies that hold a life together rarely survive in the record — string rots, knots come loose, and the net that fed a village leaves nothing behind. What we call invisible was often the thing doing the actual holding.

stories.title: Registration without a phone number on Signal will use zero-knowledge proofs
stories.summary: A proof that shows you belong without showing who you are is a small, precise kindness: trust that does not require you to hand over the thing you were protecting. The cleanest lock is the one that never has to name its key.
